name: Portuguese Empire
alt: Estado da Índia (Portuguese India, its Asian part)
United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves (1815-1822)

successors.name: Portuguese Republic (First Portuguese Republic)
successors.text: the African, Asian and island possessions left to the monarchy in 1910 as Cliopatria draws them

ledger.x: 1415: Portugal attacks and takes Ceuta, the first possession of the Portuguese Empire.
1419: the Portuguese reach Madeira.
1427: the Portuguese reach the Azores.
1462: the Cape Verde Islands are settled.
1481: João II orders the fortress of São Jorge da Mina on the Gold Coast.
1500: Cabral lands in Brazil and the Portuguese claim the coast.
1505: the Kingdom of Cochin becomes a Portuguese protectorate.
1505: Almeida begins Fort St Angelo at Cannanore.
ledger.cp: Cannanore ruler (not named on the page)

ledger.x: 1510: Albuquerque takes Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate for good on 25 November.
1511: Albuquerque captures Malacca.
1515: Albuquerque conquers Hormuz.
1521: Cliopatria adds a 28-cell patch on the north coast of Sumatra.
1526: Cliopatria adds 3 cells at Dili on Timor.
1529: the Treaty of Zaragoza gives the Moluccas to Portugal.
1529: Cliopatria drops the north-Sumatran patch.
1529: the Malacca patch shrinks from 82 to 21 cells.
1534: Salsette, Bombay, Chaul and Bassein pass to Portugal.
1535: Diu passes to Portugal.
1539: Daman is ceded to Portugal.
1549: Tomé de Sousa founds Salvador, the first capital of Brazil.
1557: the Chinese authorities allow the Portuguese to settle in Macau.
1565: Estácio de Sá founds Rio de Janeiro against the French of Guanabara Bay.
1567: the last French settlers are expelled from Guanabara Bay.
1567: Guanabara Bay passes to Portugal for good after the French are expelled (S10).
1572: Cliopatria's Brazil grows from 812 to 1,281 cells and takes in the coast to São Paulo.
1581: Philip II is recognised as king of Portugal and the Portuguese Empire passes under the Spanish crown.
1640 (1 December): João IV is acclaimed and the Portuguese Empire is Portuguese again.
1641: Malacca falls to the Dutch.
1641: the Dutch take Luanda and Benguela.
1641: the Dutch hold São Luís.
1642: the last Portuguese posts on the Gold Coast fall.
1645: the revolt of João Fernandes Vieira opens the reconquest of Dutch Brazil.
1645: the Dutch abandon São Luís.
1648 (15 August): Luanda and all Dutch forces in Angola surrender.
1654: the Dutch are expelled from Recife.
1654: Recife and the Dutch Brazil core return to Portugal (S6, final expulsion 1654).
1656: the Dutch take Colombo.
1658: the last Portuguese leave Ceylon.
1661: Bombay passes to the English crown with Catherine of Braganza's dowry.
1661: Tangier is offered to England in the dowry.
1663: the Dutch finish the conquest of the Malabar coast.
1663: Kochi passes to the Dutch and the Portuguese protectorate of Cochin ends.
1670: Cliopatria's Brazil grows by 340 cells inland (west to 60.8 W).
1677: Cliopatria's Brazil reaches 32.6 S and grows by 170 cells.
1679: Manuel Lobo founds Colónia do Sacramento opposite Buenos Aires.
1698: Fort Jesus at Mombasa falls to the Arabs of Oman.
1706: Colonia del Sacramento leaves Cliopatria's shape.
1713: Colonia del Sacramento is back in Cliopatria's shape.
1718: Cliopatria's Brazil grows by 900 cells (225,000 km2) in the gold country.
1721: Cliopatria adds 22 cells at Cuiabá.
1727: Cliopatria adds 20 cells at Itaberai in Goiás.
1734: Cliopatria adds 21 cells at Campo Grande and 8 at Matola in Mozambique.
1738: Cliopatria adds 17 cells at Palmas.
1748: Cliopatria's Brazil grows by about 300 cells to the Guapore.
1750 (13 January): the Treaty of Madrid recognises the Portuguese interior of Brazil.
1752: Mozambique becomes a separate Captaincy-General.
1754 (July): Spanish and Portuguese forces march against the Guaraní of the Seven Missions.
1756 (February): the Guaraní are crushed at Caiboaté.
1756: Spanish and Portuguese forces occupy the missions.
1759: Spain reclaims the missions.
1762: Spain captures Colonia del Sacramento in the Fantastic War.
1763: Colonia del Sacramento is returned.
1769: Portugal's last territory in Morocco ends.
1772: Cliopatria joins the points of Luanda and Benguela into one 61-cell strip.
1777 (1 October): the First Treaty of San Ildefonso fixes the Plata frontier.
1777 (1 October): Spain acknowledges Portuguese Southern Brazil and returns Santa Catarina island.
1777: Portugal holds Rio Grande do Sul again.
1778: Cliopatria's shape grows westward by 1.3 M km2.
1778 (11 March): the Treaty of El Pardo gives Annobón and Fernão Pó to Spain.
1783: the Marathas hand over Nagar Haveli after the attack on the ship Santana.
1788: the Novas Conquistas complete the territory of Goa.
ledger.cp: Dessais of Kudal, Sondas and Bhonslas

ledger.x: 1808: the court of João VI arrives in Rio de Janeiro and the empire is governed from Brazil.
1809: an Anglo-Portuguese squadron takes French Guiana and the Portuguese in Brazil hold it.
1815: the empire becomes the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves.
1816 (August): Luso-Brazilian troops invade the Banda Oriental.
1817: French Guiana returns to France.
1820: Artigas is beaten at Tacuarembó and the Banda Oriental is held.
1821 (18 July): the Banda Oriental is annexed as the province of Cisplatina.
1822: the empire is governed from Lisbon again.
1822 (7 September): Brazil declares its independence.
1859: Cliopatria drops 3,000 km2 on Flores.
1885: Cabinda becomes a Portuguese protectorate.
1891: the frontiers of Angola are fixed by treaty.
1895: Portugal annexes the Gaza Empire of southern Mozambique.
Fix fx-31 (F166), mirror of lozi-kingdom /ledger/4: 1895: Portugal occupies part of the Lozi's western territory.
1902: the pacification of the Zambezi valley ends with the Barue campaign.
Fix fx-31 (F166), mirror of lozi-kingdom /ledger/6: 1905: the occupation ends in cession.
Fix fx-31 (F166), mirror of lozi-kingdom /ledger/7: 1905: the Lozi land west of the Zambezi passes to Portuguese Angola.
1910: the monarchy falls and the Portuguese Republic takes over Portugal and its overseas territories.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Goa
wars.outcome: Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510, the Bijapuris countered, and it was recaptured on 25 November 1510; Portuguese until 1961.

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of Malacca
wars.outcome: Albuquerque had captured Malacca by July 1511; the Dutch took it in 1641.

wars.name: Dutch–Portuguese War
wars.outcome: The Portuguese expelled the Dutch from Recife in 1654 and retook Luanda on 15 August (1648); the Dutch kept Elmina (1637), the Gold Coast (1642), Malacca (1641), Ceylon (1658) and the Malabar coast (1663).

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War
wars.outcome: João IV was acclaimed on 1 December 1640; "Spain recognized Portugal's sovereignty and made peace on 13 February 1668"; Ceuta stayed Spanish (S11) and was formally ceded in exchange (S1).

wars.name: Battle of Mbwila
wars.outcome: "Portugal defeated the Kongo Kingdom in the Battle of Mbwila on 29 October, 1665."

wars.name: Guaraní War
wars.outcome: Spanish and Portuguese forces crushed the Guaraní at Caiboaté on 10 February 1756 and occupied the missions; the Treaty of Madrid was annulled in 1761 and Spain regained them.

wars.name: Fantastic War (Spain and Portugal, 1762–1763)
wars.outcome: Spain captured Colonia del Sacramento and "the treaty later required Spain to return it".

wars.name: Anglo-Portuguese capture of French Guiana
wars.outcome: "In 1809, an Anglo-Portuguese naval squadron took French Guiana" and gave it to the Portuguese in Brazil; a Portuguese presence "remained until 1817".

wars.name: Portuguese conquest of the Banda Oriental
wars.outcome: The Portuguese invaded in August 1816, occupied Montevideo on 20 January 1817, won at Tacuarembó after a three-year struggle and annexed the province as Cisplatina in 1821 (assembly of 18 July 1821).

certainty.note: Forts, factories, claims and the Brazilian interior drawn as uti possidetis are approximate throughout.

Angola and Mozambique are drawn within treaty frontiers (1885-1886 agreements, Anglo-Portuguese Treaty 1891, award of 1905), but effective occupation came only between 1895 and the early 20th century (S8, S9), so the interior is a claim.
